text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Lithuanian president Algirdas Mykolas Brazauskas arrives on an official visit to Denmark today, with visits to the Danish parliament and a number of companies, institutions and museums on his schedule.

--- One out of three crew members in the Danish merchant fleet is a foreigner and the number will increase as long as wages for foreigners remain lower than for Danes. At present 32 percent of those employed in the sector are foreigners compared to 25 percent in 1995.

--- A new government report says that more than 30,000 jobs in Denmark are threatened by growing trade with Poland and other low wage countries in Eastern Europe. The report calls for better training for low skilled Danes and more aggressive government policies.

--- Danish State Railways (DSB) is to lose its monopoly on operating trains in the future Great Belt tunnel, connecting Denmark's two main islands and due to open in the late 1990s, receiving instead a rebate on annual debt repayments to the state, with private freight transporters also gaining access to the tunnel.
